claims.summary: For a finite-dimensional subspace U of a commutative ring R over a field and r(I)=dim U-dim(U cap I): r is antitone, r(I cap J)<=r(I)+r(J)-r(I+J), the stacked restriction to ideals I_1..I_M has rank r(cap I_a)<=sum r(I_a)-sum_{a>=2} r(I_a+I_b(a)) for any b(a)<a, and if each I_a contains one of K_1..K_C the joint rank is at most sum_c r(K_c). Increments r_U(I)-r_U(I+J) are monotone in U; for ideals generated by affine spans S_a,S_b in K[x_1..x_v] with 1 not in S_a+S_b, d_a=v-dim S_a and c=dim(S_a+S_b)-dim S_a, the increment for U inside degree<=k is at most c*binom(d_a+k-1,k-1). Elementary; no exactness hypothesis.
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer with its follow-up check, including the increment form. Submodularity is standard; ideals are generated by affine spans, so restriction is ordinary substitution.
claims.rationale: Supplies the upper-bound half of Mayer-Vietoris for arbitrary polynomial spaces and ordinary restrictions, the direction selection needs.
claims.next_action: Seek lower bounds on row-linear restriction ranks to intersections so the overlap terms can be used.

claims.summary: In Braun's F2 one-level complete accuracy-3l old-affine setting over Q_{m,l}, n=2^l, if the input span of every proper block of rank>3l(k+1) contains one of C subspaces each of dimension>3l(k+1), and m ln(4C)<=k^2, k<=m, D>=6l+1, 2k(D+1)-1<=n, 4(k-1)<n, then there is no ordinary-PC refutation through degree D, whatever the number of blocks; it contains the published theorem (C<=M) and its polynomial-inventory corollary holds with C in place of the block count. At l=16 (k=302, D=107) a family with C=1 and more than 2^(771984*262063) proper blocks of rank 786529, with distinct incomparable restriction kernels, is excluded, while the published inventory condition fails at every admissible k.
claims.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer with corrections and follow-up: kernel count, coverage by composition of restrictions, unchanged removal/separation/replay, eventual clause at the uniform-lemma k, the l=16 family and comparison. A gain only for families clustered by shared spans; generic families have C close to M.
claims.rationale: Replaces the per-block inventory of Braun's common-kernel count by a shared-subspace count, a structural joint-rank saving on actual observations with the ledger unchanged.
claims.next_action: Check whether the all-prime and accuracy-dependent versions use the inventory only in the kernel count.

relationships: The submodular inequality here, with ideal-sum containment and monotonicity, implies that lemma's always-nonpositive clause; its gluing equivalence is not addressed.
Uses the containment bound (3) for the joint restriction rank.
Replaces the proper high-rank block count by the shared-subspace count in the common-kernel lemma; C<=M recovers it.
Its kernel count is a certificate of the sufficient form of the exact selection criterion with a shared-subspace rank bound.
